candidates.title: Review chained agent answers for added claims

demandEvidence.chore: Check whether later answers in a multi-agent sequence introduce claims not present in the earlier answer.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How does this not end up in a chinese whisper game, especially considering how much LLMs infer, guess, and find edge cases and whatnot everywhere?

ease.reason: A supplied pair of answers can be compared manually, but no implementation reference supports automated claim comparison.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional teams using chained language models may pay for review; this question establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic side-by-side comparison is bounded, while defining factual equivalence and useful flags remains unresolved.

autonomy.reason: Comparisons can be repeated on supplied text, but a person must set reference truth and judge flagged differences.

evidence.reason: The literal question identifies concern about inferred additions in chained LLM work, without examples or recurrence evidence.

experimentPlan.output: A side-by-side report highlighting statements in a later agent answer that are not clearly supported by the prior answer.
inputs: Two fictional consecutive agent answers on the same task
A short operator-supplied checklist of claims that must remain intact
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes a pair of consecutive answers for review.
steps: Split each answer into short factual statements.
Compare later statements with the earlier answer and the supplied checklist.
Mark additions, contradictions, and uncertain paraphrases separately.
Show each marked statement beside both source answers.
Ask a person to decide whether each mark is a real drift issue.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On fictional answer pairs with deliberately added, changed, and preserved statements, check whether the report points to the exact later text and retains both comparison passages.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies safe text and the checklist; a person determines truth and decides whether a difference matters. Do not send private work text to an unapproved service.
unverified: No supplied source documents a model or tool that reliably aligns factual claims across answers.
Useful thresholds for paraphrase versus drift are unknown.
The discussion gives no frequency, operational context, or buyer evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: this is a concrete concern but a proposed text comparison cannot establish truth or useful drift detection, and buyer demand is unvalidated.

candidates.title: Prepare app review follow-up drafts

demandEvidence.chore: Track a submitted app review and prepare a status inquiry when no update has arrived.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: It has been in “Review process started” status for 55 days, and we haven’t had any updates.

ease.reason: An operator can enter a submission date and status, but no reference supports reading the review portal.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent app developers may pay for review tracking, but one request does not establish a market.

feasibility.reason: A reminder and inquiry draft from supplied dates is bounded; useful timing and status accuracy are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A date can trigger a draft, but a person must verify status and send the inquiry.

evidence.reason: The span describes one delayed review and a request for timing, with no recurrence evidence.

experimentPlan.output: A dated reminder and neutral inquiry draft for a submitted app review with no recorded update.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator adds or updates a review entry and its expected check-in date.
steps: Store the app label and submission date entered by the operator.
Compare the operator-entered check-in date with today’s date.
If due, draft a short inquiry using only the entered status and dates.
Show the source fields beside the draft for verification.
Require a person to confirm the portal status and send or discard the inquiry.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For fictional entries with past, future, and missing check-in dates, confirm that only due complete entries produce a draft and that no unentered status is asserted.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies dates, checks the actual review portal, chooses whether the timing warrants contact, and sends any inquiry.
unverified: No review-portal access or status integration is documented.
The source describes one submission, not a recurring task across customers.
The useful reminder interval and willingness to pay are unknown.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the span supports one follow-up need, but no recurrence, portal capability, or payer is established.

candidates.title: Check weekly keyword metric rows

demandEvidence.chore: Review a weekly keyword metrics export for missing or inconsistent volume, CPC, and difficulty fields.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Runs VNCNT Labs’ Keyword Search Volume Actor on Apify every week and adds each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets.

ease.reason: The source describes a weekly sheet workflow, but no supplied implementation reference supports fetching or writing those metrics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small marketing consultants may pay for consistent keyword reports; this maker example does not establish buyers.

feasibility.reason: A fictional-row validation prototype is bounded; accurate metrics and account access are outside supported evidence.

autonomy.reason: Rows can be checked repeatedly, but a person must obtain data and resolve warnings; no execution capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The supplied context names weekly volume, CPC, difficulty and Sheets rows, but is a single maker example.

experimentPlan.output: A review table that flags missing or malformed weekly keyword metric cells before a person uses the report.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes a weekly keyword table into the prototype.
steps: Read each supplied row without contacting an external actor.
Check whether the three metric cells are present and parseable.
Mark missing or malformed cells with a plain reason.
Group the flagged rows into a review table.
Let a person correct the source data before using it.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use fictional rows with one missing value, one nonnumeric value, and one complete row; verify flags identify the exact row and cell without inventing replacement metrics.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies and validates all metrics and decides corrections; this design does not run Apify or write to Google Sheets.
unverified: No supplied reference documents parsing, scheduled execution, Apify calls, or Google Sheets writes.
The post is a maker example, not corroborated buyer demand.
Metric accuracy and source freshness are not tested by this proposed offline check.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the described workflow is concrete, but implementation support and independent evidence of demand are absent.

candidates.title: Review whether site pages still serve a purpose

demandEvidence.chore: Review a list of site pages and flag entries with no stated question answered or task served.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Before adding anything new I check whether the page already has a reason to exist. If it does not answer a question or solve something, I delete it.

ease.reason: A person can review a supplied page list, but no reference documents reliable page-purpose classification.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small web studios may pay for upkeep review; this tip does not establish buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A worksheet over operator-supplied page summaries is bounded, though useful judgments require context.

autonomy.reason: The same checklist can flag blank purpose statements, while a person must decide whether to keep or remove pages.

evidence.reason: The excerpt states a concrete keep-or-delete rule, but gives no frequency or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A page inventory that flags entries whose purpose field is blank for human review.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes or enters a small page inventory for review.
steps: Read the supplied purpose and audience fields for each row.
Flag rows where either field is blank.
Show the supplied text beside each flag.
Group complete rows separately from rows needing clarification.
Ask a person to decide whether a page should remain, change, or be removed.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On fictional rows with complete, blank, and contradictory purpose fields, check that blanks and contradictions are surfaced without the tool deciding to delete a page.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A site owner supplies context and makes every keep, edit, or delete decision; the proposed tool gives no SEO or traffic verdict.
unverified: No supplied reference supports crawling or classifying live website pages.
The source is a tip rather than a request for paid help.
The frequency and value of this review for a buyer are unknown.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: one concrete review rule is present, but the post is a tip with no repeated need or buyer evidence.

candidates.title: Draft shipment delay notices for review

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a draft dispatcher alert from an operator-supplied shipment row marked delayed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed, copy an order update into a CRM, alert a buyer when inventory drops, or send a daily report to a team channel.

ease.reason: Synthetic shipment rows make a draft alert approachable, but no reference documents live logistics intake or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small logistics operators may pay for clearer exception notices; these examples establish no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week row-to-draft prototype is bounded, while correct delay rules and event access remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A supplied row can produce a repeatable draft, but a person must verify delay status and send the notice.

evidence.reason: The source names a dispatcher alert for delayed shipments among examples, without frequency or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A concise dispatcher alert draft from one supplied shipment row that an operator has already marked delayed.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a fictional shipment row explicitly marked delayed.
steps: Read only the supplied shipment fields.
Check that the row is marked delayed by the operator.
Draft a short alert containing the shipment reference and latest supplied update.
Show the source fields beside the draft and mark missing fields.
Require a dispatcher or operator to verify status and send the alert.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For fictional delayed, on-time, and missing-status rows, confirm a draft appears only for the delayed row and repeats no detail absent from its input.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies and verifies status, confirms the recipient, and sends the alert; the proposal does not query carrier systems or message customers.
unverified: No source documents carrier events, CRM access, messaging, or retries.
The source gives examples but no actual operating case or task frequency.
The proposed draft’s usefulness and a buyer’s willingness to pay remain hypotheses.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: this is a narrow plausible experiment, but the source provides only examples and no repeated operator demand or integration support.
